name: Schedule crews and rotations
summary: Each week every district builds the crew roster for each service line: who works each seat on the fracturing shift crews, and who is on call for cementing and coiled tubing jobs. The HR coordinator brings in absences, new hires and expiring tickets, a frac field supervisor or a dispatcher drafts the roster, the dispatcher checks it against hours-of-service and overtime rules, and the district manager fills gaps and approves overtime. After the week, the district administrator compiles field time for payroll. The work is slow and error-prone because rosters, tickets, logs and time sheets sit in separate systems and spreadsheets, and short-staffed crews in 2021-2022 meant many calls for cover.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people, roughly 880 of them in the field, with 24-hour frac and coiled tubing crews on rotation and on-call cementing crews based at nine districts.
baseline.notes: About a third of weekly schedules are for fracturing crews and two thirds for cementing or coiled tubing on-call boards.

unit_of_work: one weekly crew schedule for a service line in a district
trigger: The weekly planning cycle starts for the coming week, with the latest pad programs and job bookings.
end_state: The roster has been published and run for the week, and the week's approved field time has been released to payroll.

volume.seasonality: More active crews and schedules in the winter peak and late summer to autumn; few during spring break-up, when crews are parked.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate: about 9-11 district and service line combinations each producing one roster a week.

surge.cause: Winter peak (January to mid-March) when every crew is active and cover is hardest to find

evidence.note: Crews booked through the first quarter and tight supply of field staff (step-2021); multiplier tier C.
On-call boards, hours checks, cover calls, publishing and in-week changes; about 4 hours per weekly roster.
Roster export, absences, ticket checks, course bookings and requisitions; about 1.7 hours per roster.
Frac shift crew rosters, about a third of cases.
Gap review, cover decisions, roster and time approvals; about 1.4 hours per roster.

roles.title: District administrator (field tickets and job files)

evidence.note: Compiles and checks field time for payroll; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
HRIS, field time capture and payroll
Learning management and safety ticket tracking
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Electronic field ticketing on tablets, linked to the ERP price book

steps.name: Pull next week's work forecast
steps.description: The dispatcher lists the work expected next week for the service line in the district: pad programs and frac start dates from program planning, cementing and coiled tubing jobs already booked, and rig activity that will generate calls.

error.defect_description: A pad start or rig move left out of the forecast.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Pull roster and rotation calendar
steps.description: The HR coordinator exports the current roster for the service line and district from the HRIS with each person's position, rotation (for example 14 days on and 7 off for frac crews) and next days off.

evidence.note: Rotation pattern from the organisation file (frac crews on 14 and 7); times tier C.

steps.name: Record absences and staffing changes
steps.description: The HR coordinator enters vacation, sick days, injuries on modified duty, resignations, new hires finishing orientation and recalls from layoff, so the roster shows who is really available.

error.defect_description: A sick call or resignation not entered.

evidence.note: Turnover to other industries and new recruits in 2021-2022 (step-2021). Times tier C.

steps.name: Check tickets and certificates
steps.description: The HR coordinator compares the available people with the learning system for expired or soon-to-expire tickets (H2S Alive, first aid, dangerous goods, driver licence class and medicals) and customer-required training.

error.defect_description: Expired ticket missed; worker turned away at a customer site.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code competent worker requirements and producers' site entry training requirements

next.condition: tickets current; cementing or coiled tubing crews

evidence.note: Producers qualify contractors on HSE before work (cnrl-suppliers); share of rosters with expiring tickets tier C.

steps.name: Book renewal courses
steps.description: The HR coordinator books the people with expiring tickets into the next course at the training centre or an outside provider and marks those days as unavailable on the roster.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Build frac shift crew roster
steps.description: The frac field supervisor fills every seat on each shift crew (treater, data van, pump operators, blender, sand) from the available people, balancing experience so each shift has a qualified lead in every position, and lines up crew changes with the pad schedule.

error.defect_description: A seat filled by someone without the needed sign-off.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Build cementing or coiled tubing on-call board
steps.description: The dispatcher sets up next week's on-call board for cementing or coiled tubing crews: which supervisor and operators are on call each day, who is on days off, and spare operators to cover peaks.

error.defect_description: A person scheduled on call during days off.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check hours, rest and overtime
steps.description: The dispatcher checks the draft against the hours-of-service cycle (at least three 24-hour periods off in any 24 days and 72 hours off after a permit cycle), driver logs and the monthly hours that trigger overtime, and flags people who would exceed them.

error.defect_description: A rest breach is missed and found in a log audit.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313) s.63 oil well service vehicle permit off-duty cycle; Alberta Employment Standards oilwell servicing overtime (12 hours a day or 191 hours a month)

evidence.note: Off-duty cycle under the oil well service vehicle permit (hos63) and overtime after 12 hours a day or 191 a month (ab-es-ows) are stated in the sources; step times tier C.

steps.name: Review gaps and overtime
steps.description: The district manager reviews the checked roster, the open seats, the planned overtime and the forecast work, and decides whether the week can be covered as drafted.

evidence.note: Tight supply of field staff in 2021-2022 (step-2021). Gap share tier C.

steps.name: Call workers for cover
steps.description: The dispatcher phones and texts people on days off, spare operators and other district dispatchers to fill the open seats, recording who accepts extra shifts and the overtime that creates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Decide how to run short
steps.description: The district manager decides whether to run a crew one person short where safe, ask the service line to move a job, hold a crew over within hours limits, or ask HR to recruit or recall.

evidence.note: Limits on how fast recruits can be added safely (step-2021). Shares tier C.

steps.name: Raise requisition or recall
steps.description: The HR coordinator opens a job requisition in the HRIS for the missing positions, or contacts laid-off employees on the recall list, and tells the recruiter the start date needed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Approve roster and overtime
steps.description: The district manager approves the final roster and the planned overtime and holdovers, which commits the labour budget for the week.

control.basis: District labour budget: overtime and holdovers approved by the district manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Publish the roster
steps.description: The dispatcher posts the roster on the dispatch board, texts each person their days and crew, and sends it to program planning, the other service lines and the hours-of-service coordinator.

error.defect_description: A crew member not told of a change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Handle changes during the week
steps.description: As the week runs, the dispatcher replaces people who call in sick, quit or are hurt, moves crews when pads start late or rigs move, and keeps the roster and hours check current.

error.defect_description: A change not recorded, so time is paid to the wrong crew.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313) s.63 oil well service vehicle permit off-duty cycle; Alberta Employment Standards oilwell servicing overtime (12 hours a day or 191 hours a month)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Compile field time
steps.description: After the week closes, the district administrator compiles each person's hours, travel, standby and field bonuses from the supervisors' daily time sheets and the signed field tickets into the field time capture screens.

error.defect_description: Hours or bonus codes keyed wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check hours against tickets and logs
steps.description: The district administrator compares the time entered with the field tickets and driver logs, and flags hours with no matching job, missing days and overtime that was not approved.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Resolve time discrepancies
steps.description: The district manager calls the crew supervisors about the flagged hours, decides which hours stand and has the administrator correct the entries.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Approve field time for payroll
steps.description: The district manager approves the week's field time in the HRIS, confirming hours, overtime and bonuses against the approved roster.

control.basis: Payroll internal control: manager approval of hours before pay, separate from the person who enters them

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Submit time to payroll
steps.description: The district administrator locks the approved week and releases it to the payroll team before the payroll cut-off, and answers payroll's questions about unusual codes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

exceptions.name: Expiring tickets
exceptions.description: Some crew members need ticket renewals and are booked into courses, reducing who can work.

exceptions.name: Open seats
exceptions.description: The roster cannot be filled from people on shift; the dispatcher calls for cover and the district manager decides how to run short.

exceptions.name: Time discrepancies
exceptions.description: Entered hours do not match tickets or logs and must be resolved before payroll.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from start of weekly planning to field time released to payroll
benchmarks.population: Weekly rosters at a WCSB service company district, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: planning two to three days before the week, the seven-day week itself, and two to three days to compile and approve time before the payroll cut-off.

pain_points.description: Rosters, tickets, driver logs and time sheets sit in different systems and spreadsheets, so availability and rest checks are manual.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for weekly crew rostering at a WCSB service company district in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

pain_points.description: Short staffing in 2021-2022 meant frequent calls for cover, overtime and holdovers.

evidence.note: Tight supply of field professionals and limits on safe recruiting (step-2021).

pain_points.description: Field time is re-keyed from paper or tablet time sheets and checked against tickets by hand before payroll.

sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313), section 63 (oil well service vehicle permits), version in force 2019-06-12 to 2021-06-11
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Oil well service vehicle permit: at least three 24-hour off-duty periods in any 24 days, 72 consecutive hours off before returning to standard rules, well-site standby logged as off-duty only if no work is done and it is not part of the 8-hour minimum.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Tight supply of field staff, limits on how fast recruits can be added safely, rising labour cost; prices raised for all clients in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 to offset inflation; crews booked through Q1; spring break-up affects Canadian operations; extreme cold caused delays.

sources.title: Oilwell servicing - employment standards exceptions
sources.supports: Oilwell servicing (including cementing and fracturing) overtime is paid after 12 hours a day or 191 hours a month, whichever is greater; the 12-consecutive-hour confinement rule does not apply; OHS duties on extended hours still apply.

sources.title: Prospective Suppliers
sources.supports: A producer qualifies contractors for health, safety and environment through ISNetworld before work; registration and qualification do not imply an award.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).

The trigger is the weekly cycle: fracturing rosters follow pad programs and cementing and coiled tubing on-call boards follow dispatch bookings; the organisation file lists only pad programs as the trigger.

The district administrator, who compiles field time, takes part although the process map does not list that role; new hires from hr-onboarding and training bookings to hs-training-and-competency are links the process map lacks.
The week the roster runs is modelled as calendar waits before s16 and s17; the elapsed cycle time is set mainly by that week.
Crew change travel and crew time on location are not counted here; they belong to the field execution processes.
